note: Candidate entries for guidance/principles.json. Not approved. antipatterns are empty until the owner decides whether the pattern gets its own anti-pattern or check. Updated for CaissaTrainer Phase 3 (hidden panels reserve nothing, chevron toggles, drawer before restack, task ordered stacking).

principles.title: Primary Workspace Stays Primary
principles.summary: Keep the one primary region primary; support it with hideable panels.
rules: Keep the primary region centered, never squeezed below a usable minimum, and the last to give up room.
Disclose secondary information progressively in panels the person can hide.
Center the region and its open panels as one group; a hidden panel or a drawer reserves no width.
Do not flank the region with equally prominent panels: supporting information is subordinate, and the panel the person works against has no heading or card of its own.
No zen or fullscreen mode: the largest size that fits and hiding the panels cover it.
Panels hold content, never navigation (principle 14).
Controls about the primary region live in a rail attached to it (resize handle and one options menu), not in the page toolbar; its width is reserved on both sides.
A second view of the primary object is secondary: closed by default, capped well below the primary region.

Optional tools start closed behind one control and the choice is remembered; nothing essential is hidden behind them. Which tools a module offers is a per-module decision with a stated reason, and removing one never strands what the person already wrote.

A panel is shown or hidden by a quiet chevron attached to its workspace edge (a disclosure row when stacked), reporting aria-expanded, with a 40px touch target; never a toolbar button named after the panel and never an X.
When stacked, order by task: region, status and answer controls, supporting panel, then optional tools behind a disclosure row.
exceptions: Applications whose product is a feed, a table or a document with a reading measure and no single primary region.

principles.title: Panels Yield Before Content
principles.summary: When space runs out, panels shrink, then become a drawer, then stack.
rules: The optional panel yields to a drawer before the layout restacks (the region never drops below a stated comfort minimum, 400px in the reference); the panel the person works against yields last.
In a portrait window stack when stacking gives a much bigger region (under 70 percent of the stacked size beside the panels); never stack a landscape window only because stacking would be bigger.
Order of yielding: shrink to the minimum width, on-demand drawer, stack under the primary region on a narrow screen.
Never delete a panel to make room; never leave a hidden panel without a visible control that restores it.
A drawer closes with Escape and returns focus to the control that opened it.
Keep panels mounted so their state survives.
The responsive default is sized against the open panels' minimum widths so panels yield first and grow into what remains; the default never turns the supporting panel into a drawer.
An open drawer is a modal dialog: background inert, focus contained, Escape closes only it, focus returns to the chevron that opened it; its own control is a back chevron, not an X.

principles.title: Layout Choices Are Preferences
principles.summary: A chosen size or panel state is stored as the choice, never as a measurement.
rules: Store the choice, not the clamped value; a smaller window never rewrites it.
Offer one control that restores the defaults.
Remember panel visibility per screen; share one size between compatible screens; keep it device-local unless the choice concerns the account.
Guard storage access and fall back to defaults.

principles.title: Do Not Fix the Size of Central Content
principles.summary: The primary region has a responsive medium default and the person can resize it.
rules: No fixed pixel size for the primary region of a workspace.
The default is dominant but deliberately below the maximum (capped at 720px in the reference); the person can go larger or smaller.
The resize handle is a slider in the control rail: arrow keys, Home and End, 40px touch target.
Measure the chrome around the region and hold its peak so the region does not jump.
exceptions: Text with a reading measure keeps its maximum line length.
A preview that must show true size (principle 22, documented exception).
